text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- GOV'T CREATES EXPORT INCENTIVES

Brazil's Central Bank announced new rules allowing banks to raise capital overseas to lend to exporters. Financial institutions will be able to place bonds abroad and use the resources to lend capital to Brazilian exporters with 180-day maturities.
-- INDUSTRIAL SALES RECOVER
Industrial activity resumed growth in July, according to the National Industry Confederation (CNI). Industry sales rose 8.05 percent last month, when compared with June.
Between January and July, industry sales were 1.47 percent higher than during the same period last year, the first time in 1996 that accumulated sales have topped last year's comparative levels.
-- VALE TO BE PRIVATIZED IN THREE PHASES
The government announced Thursday the privatization model for mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD). A 51 percent stake belonging to the federal government will be offered in three phases.

The privatization will begin in February 1997 with a block sale of 40-45 percent of voting shares. After the block sale, 10 percent of CVRD's total capital will be offered to staff and a public offering on international and domestic markets would follow from June 1997 on.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- INCOME DISTRIBUTION IMPROVES

Distribution of income has improved in Brazil, according to the National Statistics Institute (IBGE). The poorest 10 percent of the population accounted for 1.1 percent of the country's total wealth in 1995, up from 0.7 percent in 1993.
That means a record since the Cruzado Plan in 1986, when the poorest accounted for one percent.
-- MENEM'S POPULARITY FALLS TO 20 PCT
Popularity of Argentina's President Carlos Menem fell to 20 percent. According to a poll, 58 percent of the Argentines don't believe in an economic pick-up this year.
O GLOBO
-- USE OF FGTS FUNDS WILL BE ALLOWED IN VALE'S SELLOFF
The National Privatization Council (CND) approved Thursday the use of FGTS funds by workers in the privatization of mining giant Vale do Rio Doce, scheduled to begin in February 1997.
-- RIO'S CHEMICAL COMPLEX APPROVED BY PETROBRAS
Petrobras approved a contract which will make it viable the construction of a gas-chemical complex in Duque de Caxias.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo newsroom, 55-11-2324411
